metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Cron
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Cron APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that schedules a one-time event at the supplied timestamp for the hook 'wpbp_single_event' only when that hook is not already scheduled.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_cron_001()` uses `wp_next_scheduled()` to avoid enqueueing another `wpbp_single_event`, schedules exactly one one-time event with `wp_schedule_single_event()` when none exists, and returns false without changing the existing timestamp on later calls.
requirements: Use wp_next_scheduled() to detect an existing event
Return false when the hook already has a scheduled event

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_001' ) ) { return false; } $first = time() + HOUR_IN_SECONDS; $second = $first + HOUR_IN_SECONDS; $scheduled = wpbp_cron_001( $first ); $first_timestamp = wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_single_event' ); $blocked = wpbp_cron_001( $second ); return true === $scheduled && $first === $first_timestamp && false === $blocked && $first === wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_single_event' );
assertions.description: The first call schedules the single event, while a later call leaves the existing timestamp unchanged

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_001( int $timestamp ): bool { if ( false !== wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_single_event' ) ) { return false; } return wp_schedule_single_event( $timestamp, 'wpbp_single_event' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that schedules the hook 'wpbp_hourly_event' as an hourly recurring event starting at the supplied timestamp and using the provided argument array.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_cron_002()` schedules `wpbp_hourly_event` with `wp_schedule_event()` using the `hourly` recurrence and the provided argument array. Runtime validation inspects the scheduled event object for the timestamp, recurrence name, interval, and stored arguments.
requirements: Use wp_schedule_event() with the hourly recurrence
Pass the provided argument array to the scheduled event

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_002' ) ) { return false; } $ts = time() + HOUR_IN_SECONDS; $args = array( 'site' => 'wp-bench' ); $result = wpbp_cron_002( $ts, $args ); $event = wp_get_scheduled_event( 'wpbp_hourly_event', $args ); return true === $result && $event && $ts === $event->timestamp && 'hourly' === $event->schedule && HOUR_IN_SECONDS === $event->interval && $args === $event->args;
assertions.description: The hourly cron event is scheduled with the requested timestamp, interval, and arguments

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_002( int $timestamp, array $args ): bool { return wp_schedule_event( $timestamp, 'hourly', 'wpbp_hourly_event', $args ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that unschedules only the next event for the hook 'wpbp_unschedule' that matches the provided argument array.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_cron_003()` finds the next scheduled `wpbp_unschedule` event for the provided arguments with `wp_next_scheduled()` and removes that timestamp with `wp_unschedule_event()`. Runtime validation schedules two matching events and verifies only the earlier event is removed.
requirements: Find the next matching timestamp with wp_next_scheduled()
Unschedule that timestamp with the same hook and arguments

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_003' ) ) { return false; } $args = array( 'id' => 31 ); $first = time() + 1000; $second = $first + HOUR_IN_SECONDS; wp_schedule_single_event( $first, 'wpbp_unschedule', $args ); wp_schedule_single_event( $second, 'wpbp_unschedule', $args ); $result = wpbp_cron_003( $args ); return true === $result && $second === wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_unschedule', $args );
assertions.description: Only the next matching cron event is unscheduled

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_003( array $args ): bool { $timestamp = wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_unschedule', $args ); if ( false === $timestamp ) { return false; } return wp_unschedule_event( $timestamp, 'wpbp_unschedule', $args ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that adds a custom recurrence named 'wpbp_five_minutes' to WordPress cron schedules with a 300-second interval and display text 'Every five minutes'.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_cron_004()` attaches a `cron_schedules` filter that adds `wpbp_five_minutes` while preserving existing schedules. Runtime validation retrieves the schedules through WordPress and verifies the custom interval and display label.

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_004' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_cron_004(); $schedules = wp_get_schedules(); return isset( $schedules['wpbp_five_minutes'] ) && 300 === $schedules['wpbp_five_minutes']['interval'] && 'Every five minutes' === $schedules['wpbp_five_minutes']['display'];
assertions.description: The custom five-minute cron recurrence is available through wp_get_schedules()

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_004(): void { add_filter( 'cron_schedules', function ( $schedules ) { $schedules['wpbp_five_minutes'] = array( 'interval' => 300, 'display' => 'Every five minutes' ); return $schedules; } ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that attempts scheduling the hook 'wpbp_invalid_event' with the invalid recurrence slug 'wpbp_missing_schedule' and returns the WP_Error object produced by WordPress.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_cron_005()` calls `wp_schedule_event()` with WordPress error returns enabled for a recurrence that is not registered. Runtime validation expects the returned object to be a `WP_Error` with the `invalid_schedule` code and no scheduled `wpbp_invalid_event` event.
requirements: Enable WP_Error returns when calling wp_schedule_event()
Return the error object instead of converting it to a boolean

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_005' ) ) { return false; } $result = wpbp_cron_005(); return is_wp_error( $result ) && 'invalid_schedule' === $result->get_error_code() && false === wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_invalid_event' );
assertions.description: Invalid recurrence scheduling returns WordPress' invalid_schedule error and does not enqueue an event

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_005(): WP_Error { return wp_schedule_event( time() + HOUR_IN_SECONDS, 'wpbp_missing_schedule', 'wpbp_invalid_event', array(), true ); }

tests.prompt: A plugin is being deactivated and must leave no scheduled work behind. Implement a function that cancels every scheduled event for a given hook — including the events that were scheduled with different argument sets — and returns how many events it removed. Events registered on other hooks must survive.
tests.expected_behavior: Cancelling by hook name alone requires `wp_unschedule_hook()`, which returns the number of events removed across all argument sets; `wp_clear_scheduled_hook( $hook )` only clears the events whose arguments are the empty array. Runtime validation schedules the same hook with two different argument sets and once with no arguments, plus one event on a second hook, then checks the return value is 3, that all three are gone, that the other hook survives, and that a second call returns 0.
requirements: Cancel every scheduled event for the supplied hook, whatever arguments it was scheduled with
Return the number of events that were removed
Leave events on other hooks scheduled

required_patterns.description: Clears the hook across all argument sets

runtime_checks.setup: wp_unschedule_hook( 'wpbp_purge_cache' ); wp_unschedule_hook( 'wpbp_keep_cache' ); $now = time(); wp_schedule_single_event( $now + 3600, 'wpbp_purge_cache', array( 'site-1' ) ); wp_schedule_single_event( $now + 7200, 'wpbp_purge_cache', array( 'site-2' ) ); wp_schedule_single_event( $now + 10800, 'wpbp_purge_cache' ); wp_schedule_single_event( $now + 3600, 'wpbp_keep_cache', array( 'site-1' ) );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_006' ) ) { return false; } if ( false === wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_purge_cache', array( 'site-1' ) ) ) { return false; } $removed = wpbp_cron_006( 'wpbp_purge_cache' ); if ( 3 !== $removed ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_purge_cache', array( 'site-1' ) ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_purge_cache', array( 'site-2' ) ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_purge_cache' ) ) { return false; } if ( ! is_int( wp_next_scheduled( 'wpbp_keep_cache', array( 'site-1' ) ) ) ) { return false; } return 0 === wpbp_cron_006( 'wpbp_purge_cache' );
assertions.description: All three argument sets are cancelled, the other hook survives, and a repeat call removes nothing

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_006( string $hook ): int { $removed = wp_unschedule_hook( $hook ); return is_int( $removed ) ? $removed : 0; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_cron_006( string $hook ): int { $removed = wp_clear_scheduled_hook( $hook ); return is_int( $removed ) ? $removed : 0; }
function wpbp_cron_006( string $hook ): int { $count = 0; while ( false !== ( $timestamp = wp_next_scheduled( $hook ) ) ) { wp_unschedule_event( $timestamp, $hook ); ++$count; } return $count; }

tests.prompt: A status screen shows what WordPress has queued for one hook and one exact argument set. Implement a function that, given a hook and its argument array, returns an array with 'timestamp' (the Unix timestamp of the next run), 'schedule' (the recurrence name, or false for a one-off event) and 'interval' (the recurrence length in seconds, 0 for a one-off event). Return false when nothing is scheduled for that hook with exactly those arguments.
tests.expected_behavior: `wp_next_scheduled()` only exposes the timestamp, so the recurrence has to come from `wp_get_scheduled_event()`, whose returned object carries `schedule` (false for single events) and an `interval` that is only set for recurring events. Runtime validation registers an hourly event with one argument set and a single event with another, then checks both shapes, an unknown argument set and an unknown hook.
requirements: Match the event by hook and by the exact argument array
Report 'timestamp', 'schedule' and 'interval', with schedule false and interval 0 for a one-off event
Return false when no event is scheduled for that hook and argument set

runtime_checks.setup: wp_unschedule_hook( 'wpbp_sync_feed' ); $now = time(); $recurring = $now + 1800; $single = $now + 900; wp_schedule_event( $recurring, 'hourly', 'wpbp_sync_feed', array( 'alpha' ) ); wp_schedule_single_event( $single, 'wpbp_sync_feed', array( 'beta' ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_cron_007_times'] = array( 'recurring' => $recurring, 'single' => $single );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_cron_007' ) ) { return false; } $times = (array) ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_cron_007_times'] ?? array() ); if ( 2 !== count( $times ) ) { return false; } $recurring = wpbp_cron_007( 'wpbp_sync_feed', array( 'alpha' ) ); if ( ! is_array( $recurring ) ) { return false; } if ( (int) $times['recurring'] !== ( $recurring['timestamp'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( 'hourly' !== ( $recurring['schedule'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( 3600 !== ( $recurring['interval'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } $single = wpbp_cron_007( 'wpbp_sync_feed', array( 'beta' ) ); if ( ! is_array( $single ) ) { return false; } if ( (int) $times['single'] !== ( $single['timestamp'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== ( $single['schedule'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( 0 !== ( $single['interval'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== wpbp_cron_007( 'wpbp_sync_feed', array( 'gamma' ) ) ) { return false; } return false === wpbp_cron_007( 'wpbp_missing_feed', array( 'alpha' ) );
assertions.description: Recurring and one-off events report distinct shapes and unknown argument sets report nothing

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_cron_007( string $hook, array $args ) { $event = wp_get_scheduled_event( $hook, $args ); if ( ! $event ) { return false; } return array( 'timestamp' => (int) $event->timestamp, 'schedule' => $event->schedule, 'interval' => isset( $event->interval ) ? (int) $event->interval : 0 ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_cron_007( string $hook, array $args ) { $timestamp = wp_next_scheduled( $hook, $args ); if ( false === $timestamp ) { return false; } return array( 'timestamp' => (int) $timestamp, 'schedule' => 'hourly', 'interval' => 3600 ); }

function wpbp_cron_007( string $hook, array $args ) { $event = wp_get_scheduled_event( $hook ); if ( ! $event ) { return false; } return array( 'timestamp' => (int) $event->timestamp, 'schedule' => $event->schedule, 'interval' => isset( $event->interval ) ? (int) $event->interval : 0 ); }
